_source: OrderStatus.java — the enum the backend actually moves an order through — and PaymentStatus.java for the money column. The labels are plain English for the same states; the `status` field is the real constant, so a reader can match what they see in the app to what is written here.
_why: Every delivery site says 'track your order'. Almost none say what the states ARE, which is the thing a customer is actually asking when an order sits on one for ten minutes. These are the real ones, in the real order, including the three that are not part of a happy path.

happy.label: Order placed
happy.detail: Payment authorised and the shop is notified. Nothing is captured yet.

happy.label: Shop accepted
happy.detail: The shop has your items and has confirmed it can fulfil them.

happy.label: Rider assigned
happy.detail: A partner nearby took the job. They can see the shop, you, and the distance between all three before accepting.

happy.label: Picked up
happy.detail: Collected from the shop and on the way.

happy.label: Out for delivery
happy.detail: Live on the map until it reaches you.

happy.label: Delivered
happy.detail: Confirmed with a one-time code you give the rider — not a tap on their phone.

unhappy.label: Cancelled
unhappy.detail: Before pickup, by you or by the shop. Anything authorised is released.

unhappy.label: Refund started
unhappy.detail: Raised against the original payment, with a reference you can quote.

unhappy.label: Refunded
unhappy.detail: Back on the card or account it came from.
